long_biography.plain_text:
Grupo Televisa emerged when Telesistema Mexicano, the family-controlled broadcaster inherited by Emilio Azcárraga Milmo, merged with Televisión Independiente de México. Azcárraga became the combined group's forceful operator, using its national television base to build a vertically integrated media business. Production, publishing, radio, music and satellite distribution extended the value of the inherited platform.

His defining strategy was internationalisation. Televisa exported telenovelas and entertainment to Europe, invested in the Spanish International Communications Corporation in the United States, and launched Galavisión and ECO through satellite links. The model turned Mexican programmes into reusable assets for Spanish-speaking audiences beyond Mexico. The expansion made him Latin America's leading media proprietor. He remained chairman until shortly before his death, when control passed to his son.

uncertainties.detail: Azcárraga was born in San Antonio and some tertiary sources describe him as both Mexican and American, but the stronger sources reviewed consistently frame him as a Mexican executive without directly documenting dual citizenship. The existing Mexican nationality is retained and no secondary nationality is proposed.

The original radio and television platform came from his father, so Founder or any self-made origin would misstate the transfer. Official company history and independent reporting document a material merger, international distribution and satellite expansion under Azcárraga Milmo, supporting Inherited and expanded with an Operator relationship.

One contemporary obituary gives an anomalous earlier year for his father's death. The official Televisa chronology, specialist reference biography, broadcast encyclopedia and later reporting consistently place succession around the father's 1972 death and Televisa's 1973 formation; the dossier follows that stronger consensus without adding an exact succession year to the short biography.

The owner record stores the United States as main residence, while public business histories centre his career in Mexico and report residences and treatment abroad. Residence ordering is not necessary to the biography and no correction is proposed.
